label: lem:continuous_at_interior
title: Continuity at interior points
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $\texttt{uIcc}\; a\; b = [\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, and let $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{ContinuousAt}\; f\; x$). This follows because $x$ is an interior point of $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, so the closed interval is a neighborhood of $x$, and \texttt{ContinuousOn} at a point where the set is a neighborhood implies \texttt{ContinuousAt} (via \texttt{ContinuousWithinAt.continuousAt}).
proof: Since $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\;(\min\, a\, b)\;(\max\, a\, b)$, the closed interval $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ is a neighborhood of $x$ (by \texttt{Icc\_mem\_nhds}). Therefore $\texttt{ContinuousOn}\; f\; ([\min(a,b), \max(a,b)])$ at $x$ upgrades to $\texttt{ContinuousAt}\; f\; x$.
